sub_graphs.title: Fulu: Validator Custody Group State Transitions
sub_graphs.description: Models the lifecycle of validator custody group management, including how custody requirements are calculated, advertised, and persisted across restarts

nodes.label: Validator Active with Balance
nodes.description: Validator is active on the beacon chain with an effective balance that determines custody requirements

nodes.label: Compute Custody Requirement
nodes.description: Calculate custody group count via get_validators_custody_requirement(): total validator balance / BALANCE_PER_ADDITIONAL_CUSTODY_GROUP (32 ETH), clamped between VALIDATOR_CUSTODY_REQUIREMENT (8) and NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS

nodes.label: Custody Requirement Determined
nodes.description: System has computed the number of custody groups this validator must maintain

nodes.label: Check If Custody Count Increased
nodes.description: Compare newly computed custody requirement against previously advertised custody_group_count to determine if an increase occurred

nodes.label: Custody Count Increased
nodes.description: New custody requirement exceeds previously advertised count; validator must immediately advertise the updated count

nodes.label: Custody Count Not Increased
nodes.description: New custody requirement is equal to or less than previously advertised count; validator MUST NOT reduce advertised count

nodes.label: Advertise Updated Custody Group Count
nodes.description: Immediately advertise the updated custody_group_count to the network; this count must persist as the highest value across restarts

nodes.label: Custody Count Advertised
nodes.description: Validator is advertising its custody group count to the network and persists the highest value across restarts

ambiguities.text: The specification states validators must 'immediately advertise updated custody_group_count' on increases but does not specify what 'immediately' means in terms of timing guarantees or network propagation.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume 'immediately' means within the same epoch boundary or as soon as the custody computation completes, before the next attestation duty. This is an assumption that needs verification.

ambiguities.text: The spec says validators 'MUST hold on to sidecars for MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS_REQUESTS' and 'serve when capable' - the phrase 'when capable' is undefined.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume 'when capable' means whenever the validator node is online and has the data available in local storage, with no requirement to guarantee 100% uptime for serving. This is an assumption.

ambiguities.text: The BlobsBundle structure is described as containing 'proofs (now cell KZG proofs)' but the exact transition from blob proofs to cell KZG proofs and backward compatibility is not detailed.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume the Fulu fork replaces blob-level KZG proofs entirely with cell-level KZG proofs in the BlobsBundle, with no backward compatibility required post-fork activation.

ambiguities.text: The specification does not define behavior when get_data_column_sidecars_from_column_sidecar() receives an invalid or malformed sidecar for reconstruction.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume the function will fail or return an error if the input sidecar is invalid, and the caller is responsible for validating sidecar integrity before attempting reconstruction.

implicit_assumptions.description: The custody_group_count advertised by a validator is trusted by peers to be accurate and not inflated or deflated for strategic advantage.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: A validator could advertise a lower custody count to reduce storage/bandwidth obligations, degrading data availability guarantees. Conversely, inflating could cause peers to over-rely on that node.

implicit_assumptions.description: Validators have sufficient local storage to retain all DataColumnSidecars for their custody groups during the full MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS_REQUESTS retention period.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Storage exhaustion could cause validators to prune sidecars early, reducing data availability and potentially breaking reconstruction for sampling nodes.

implicit_assumptions.description: An attacker cannot reconstruct all columns from a subset of columns below the data availability sampling threshold, meaning the erasure coding provides sufficient redundancy guarantees.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: If reconstruction is possible from fewer columns than expected, the data availability guarantee weakens and a block producer could withhold data while still passing sampling checks.

implicit_assumptions.description: The monotonically increasing custody_group_count (never reduced, persisted across restarts) assumes validators will not need to legitimately reduce their custody obligations even if their balance decreases significantly.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Validators whose balance drops significantly are stuck serving more custody groups than required, increasing their operational burden disproportionately to their stake, potentially incentivizing node shutdown instead of continued operation.

implicit_assumptions.description: The execution layer's GetPayloadResponse (containing blobs bundle with cell KZG proofs) is assumed to provide correct and honestly-generated cell proofs.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: A compromised or buggy execution layer client could produce invalid cell KZG proofs, causing validators to distribute invalid sidecars and potentially triggering consensus failures or data availability issues.
